source_caption:
🎬 Driving Miss Daisy (1989)

Driving Miss Daisy follows Daisy Werthan, an elderly Jewish widow living in Atlanta, Georgia, whose son hires Hoke Colburn, an African-American chauffeur, after she becomes unable to drive safely. Initially resistant to accepting his assistance, Daisy treats Hoke with skepticism and stubbornness. However, over the course of twenty-five years, their relationship gradually develops into a meaningful and unexpected friendship. As they navigate personal challenges, cultural differences, and the changing social landscape of the American South, they develop a deep understanding and respect for one another. Starring Jessica Tandy and Morgan Freeman, the film delivers powerful performances and heartfelt storytelling while exploring friendship, racial prejudice, aging, dignity, compassion, and the importance of looking beyond social and cultural differences.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Comedy

⭐ IMDb: 7.3/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 39m • PG

🎥 Director: Bruce Beresford

✍️ Writer: Alfred Uhry

🏆 Awards: 4 Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Actress.

source_details.synopsis: Driving Miss Daisy is a 1989 American comedy drama film directed by Bruce Beresford and written by Alfred Uhry, based on Uhry's 1987 play. The film stars Jessica Tandy, Morgan Freeman, and Dan Aykroyd. Freeman reprised his role from the original Off-Broadway production. The story defines Daisy and her point of view—through a network of relationships and emotions by focusing on her home life, synagogue, friends, family, fears, and concerns—over a twenty-five-year period.
